coverage.category: 31. Country-specific: Small Business Tax and cash-book regime for non-resident individual traders
coverage.found: Key finding. SBT is 3.5% of quarterly gross sales (2.5% in older sheets); due 15 Oct/Jan/Apr/Jul; a cash book and a wages register are required; NRO runs record-keeping audits; the NRO issues cash-book templates for retail, restaurant, vehicle rental and vehicle repair, with Chinese translations; there is no online portal. coverage.found: Gaming Regulations: bingo fee 15% of prize value (AUD 100 if minimal prizes), betting AUD 10,000 per premises per 12 months (2016 schedule); issued by the NRO Revenue Division. Tiny, few operators. Weak.

coverage.category: 35. Country-specific: Liquor Control Act licensing (bar, restaurant, off-licence, club)
coverage.found: Licence classes (bar, restaurant, nightclub, off-licence, club, special event, liquor import); Forms and Fees Regulations 2021 amended in May 2025 (bar and restaurant application AUD 3,000). Few licensees. Weak.

coverage.category: 36. Country-specific: Cash export licence (AUD 5,000+ cash export, Customs and NRO Revenue Division)
coverage.found: Customs order from 2023 bars export of AUD 5,000 or more without written approval; the NRO publishes an application form. Individual one-off permit. Not a software workflow.

coverage.category: 37. Country-specific: Immigration local business (employment) visa, employer sponsor duties (Immigration Regulations 2023)
coverage.found: Employer must justify the foreign hire, visa is tied to the employer; visa fee cannot be waived. Small employers apply case by case. Weak.

coverage.found: AML-TFS Act 2023, Record Keeping Regulations 2023, Beneficial Ownership Act 2017 and Corporations Regulations 2018; the buyers are a handful of agents. Sources conflict; unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03 and nothing viable. Nauru has no reticulated water network. Supply is desalination (state utility, tanker delivery; 2021 RO plant, 1800 m3/d), household rainwater tanks and brackish groundwater. The water sector is state-run (Nauru Utilities Corporation, formerly Authority). A 2010 stocktake lists only RonPhos and NRC as commercial water-delivery entities. I found no licensing regime for private desalination or tanker operators (the 2001 plan only says private desalination units are allowed and tankers must be kept clean). The ADB-funded project is meant to update water and sanitation regulatory codes, so a permit regime may emerge. No well-driller or abstraction-permit register found. Island of about 12,000 people, so no private buyer group.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Solid waste is a state service. NRC (Nauru Rehabilitation Corporation) collects weekly and free; households buy a 240L bin for about AUD 108. Japan donated two garbage trucks and two compactors in Nov 2025. No private waste haulers found. Sanitation is on-site (many septic tanks leaking, septage plants over capacity), and the ADB Sustainable and Resilient Urban Development Project (USD 37.5M grant approved Sept 2024) covers sanitation, composting and recycling, and tariff and cost-recovery updates. No private septic hauler licensing or register found, and no private buyer group. Not verified whether private septic desludging operators exist.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: The Funeral, Burial and Cremation Act 2017 (No. 27 of 2017, certified 19 Dec 2017, repealed the Cemeteries Act 1922) sets up a Funeral, Burial and Cremation Committee. It covers who controls funerals, disposal within 24 hours, burial at sea, cremation (with fees), a ban on home burials, health-practitioner certificates and burial of destitute persons. It regulates cemeteries and facilities for disposing of remains. The Act's full text could not be opened (AustLII returned HTTP 503 twice), so I could not confirm whether private funeral operators are licensed or must keep registers. No private funeral operators found in search. Likely very few operators, government or family-run, so buyer pool is negligible.

result.reason: Duty is real: non-resident individuals liable to Small Business Tax must file the NRO Business Tax Quarterly Return and pay within 15 days of each quarter end (15 Oct, Jan, Apr, Jul). The form states 3.5% of gross revenue; a third-party guide says 2.5%, so the rate is unresolved. I found no online portal or e-filing. Filing is by PDF form, email or in person at the Revenue Office. No Nauru-specific app was found. I could not read the seminar PDF (binary), so cash-book rules, penalties and the 1 July 2026 change are unchecked. The market is tiny (probably a few hundred filers, no register found). Willingness to pay is low because free NRO templates exist. The Nauru-specific demand is too small for a solo founder.
